sonnet.problem: This story card sets up the fill-in-the-blank on card 12 by saying He gives Himself, 'paying the price to set people free.' That is the meaning of 'ransom,' so it hands the baker the answer to the next choice card. It also adds 'to set people free,' which verse 6 does not say.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

sonnet.problem: The card closes by saying Paul 'finishes with a word he already used earlier, when he talked about how the women dress.' Card 3 had already shown 'self-control' in the dress verse. This points straight at the right answer to the fill-in-the-blank on card 12.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

sonnet.problem: Adam and Eve show up here for the first time in the passage with no short label saying who they are.
sonnet.rule: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."
